units.rightText: He said to them, “You know how unlawful it is for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him. But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean.

units.rightText: So when I was invited, I came without objection. I ask, then, why have you sent for me?”

units.rightText: Therefore send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea.’

units.rightText: All the prophets testify about Him that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.”

units.rightText: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.

units.leftText: If then God gave to them the same gift as us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?”
units.rightText: So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to hinder the work of God?”

units.leftText: When they heard these things, they held their peace and glorified God, saying, “Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!”
units.rightText: When they heard this, they had no further objections, and they glorified God, saying, “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life.”

units.rightText: So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was fervently praying to God for him.

units.leftText: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Stand up quickly!” His chains fell off his hands.
units.rightText: Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his wrists.

units.rightText: “Get dressed and put on your sandals,” said the angel. Peter did so, and the angel told him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”

units.rightText: So Peter followed him out, but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision.

units.leftText: When they were past the first and the second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened to them by itself. They went out and went down one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.
units.rightText: They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself. When they had gone outside and walked the length of one block, the angel suddenly left him.

units.leftText: When Peter had come to himself, he said, “Now I truly know that the Lord has sent out his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from everything the Jewish people were expecting.”
units.rightText: Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for sure that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating.”

units.rightText: And when he had realized this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered together and were praying.

units.leftText: But Peter continued knocking. When they had opened, they saw him and were amazed.
units.rightText: But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.

units.leftText: whom he gathered together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.

units.leftText: You see and hear that not at Ephesus alone, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away many people, saying that they are no gods that are made with hands.

units.leftText: Not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.”
units.rightText: There is danger not only that our business will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be discredited and her majesty deposed — she who is worshiped by all the province of Asia and the whole world.”

units.rightText: When the men heard this, they were enraged and began shouting, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

units.leftText: The whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.
units.rightText: Soon the whole city was in disarray. They rushed together into the theatre, dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s traveling companions from Macedonia.

units.leftText: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another, for the assembly was in confusion. Most of them didn’t know why they had come together.

units.rightText: But when they realized that he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

units.leftText: When the town clerk had quieted the multitude, he said, “You men of Ephesus, what man is there who doesn’t know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of the image which fell down from Zeus?
units.rightText: Finally the city clerk quieted the crowd and declared, “Men of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?

units.leftText: Seeing then that these things can’t be denied, you ought to be quiet and to do nothing rash.
units.rightText: Since these things are undeniable, you ought to be calm and not do anything rash.

units.leftText: For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of your goddess.
units.rightText: For you have brought these men here, though they have neither robbed our temple nor blasphemed our goddess.

units.rightText: So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and proconsuls are available. Let them bring charges against one another there.

units.leftText: But if you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.
units.rightText: But if you are seeking anything beyond this, it must be settled in a legal assembly.

units.leftText: For indeed we are in danger of being accused concerning today’s riot, there being no cause. Concerning it, we wouldn’t be able to give an account of this commotion.”
units.rightText: For we are in jeopardy of being charged with rioting for today’s events, and we have no justification to account for this commotion.”

units.leftText: When he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
units.rightText: After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.

units.leftText: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
units.rightText: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.

units.leftText: When he had gone through those parts and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.
units.rightText: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement, he arrived in Greece,

units.rightText: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.

units.rightText: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak, he departed.

units.leftText: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.
units.rightText: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive.

units.rightText: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.

units.rightText: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.

units.rightText: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.

units.leftText: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;

units.leftText: how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,
units.rightText: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,

units.leftText: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus.
units.rightText: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
rightNotes: 20:21 ECM, TR, and Tischendorf; SBL, NE, BYZ, and WH our Lord Jesus

units.leftText: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;

units.leftText: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.

units.leftText: But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.
units.rightText: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus — the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.

units.leftText: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.
units.rightText: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.

units.leftText: Therefore I testify to you today that I am clean from the blood of all men,
units.rightText: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men.

units.leftText: for I didn’t shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.
units.rightText: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God.

units.leftText: Take heed, therefore, to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Lord and God which he purchased with his own blood.
units.rightText: Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.
rightNotes: 20:28 Tischendorf of the Lord; BYZ and PT of the Lord and God

units.leftText: For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
units.rightText: I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.

units.leftText: Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.
units.rightText: Even from your own number, men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.

units.leftText: Therefore watch, remembering that for a period of three years I didn’t cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.
units.rightText: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.

units.leftText: Now, brothers, I entrust you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
units.rightText: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.

units.leftText: I coveted no one’s silver, gold, or clothing.

units.leftText: You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.
units.rightText: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.

units.leftText: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”
units.rightText: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

units.leftText: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
units.rightText: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.

units.leftText: They all wept freely, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,
units.rightText: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.

units.leftText: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
units.rightText: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

units.leftText: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
units.rightText: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.

units.rightText: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.

units.leftText: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.
units.rightText: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.

units.leftText: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.
units.rightText: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.

units.rightText: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day.

units.rightText: After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

units.rightText: Then Paul answered, “Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

units.rightText: After these days, we packed up and went on to Jerusalem.

units.rightText: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.

units.rightText: Therefore do what we advise you. There are four men with us who have taken a vow.

units.rightText: Take these men, purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses so they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you, but that you also live in obedience to the law.

units.rightText: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.”

units.rightText: especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.

units.leftText: “Indeed, all the Jews know my way of life from my youth up, which was from the beginning among my own nation and at Jerusalem;
units.rightText: Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from my earliest childhood among my own people, and also in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
units.rightText: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.

units.leftText: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,
units.rightText: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers,

units.leftText: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!
units.rightText: the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God day and night. It is because of this hope, O king, that I am accused by the Jews.

units.leftText: Why is it judged incredible with you if God does raise the dead?
units.rightText: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?

units.leftText: “I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
units.rightText: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

units.leftText: I also did this in Jerusalem. I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.
units.rightText: And that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.

units.leftText: Punishing them often in all the synagogues, I tried to make them blaspheme. Being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
units.rightText: I frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and I tried to make them blaspheme. In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.

units.leftText: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,
units.rightText: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

units.leftText: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.
units.rightText: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and my companions.

units.leftText: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
units.rightText: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
rightNotes: 26:14 Or in Aramaic; literally in the Hebrew language

units.leftText: “I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’
units.rightText: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked.

units.leftText: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen and of the things which I will reveal to you;
units.rightText: ‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen from Me and what I will show you.

units.leftText: delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,
units.rightText: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them

units.leftText: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’
units.rightText: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.’

units.leftText: “Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
units.rightText: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.

units.leftText: but declared first to them of Damascus, at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
units.rightText: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone in the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of their repentance.

units.leftText: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.
units.rightText: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.
rightNotes: 26:21 Literally the temple

units.leftText: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would happen,
units.rightText: But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:

units.leftText: how the Christ must suffer, and how, by the resurrection of the dead, he would be first to proclaim light both to these people and to the Gentiles.”
units.rightText: that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.”

units.leftText: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!”
units.rightText: At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”

units.leftText: But he said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.
units.rightText: But Paul answered, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.

units.leftText: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.
units.rightText: For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. I am confident that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.

units.leftText: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”
units.rightText: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”

units.leftText: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”
units.rightText: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”

units.leftText: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”
units.rightText: “Short time or long,” Paul replied, “I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what I am, except for these chains.”

units.leftText: The king rose up with the governor and Bernice, and those who sat with them.
units.rightText: Then the king and the governor rose, along with Bernice and those seated with them.

units.leftText: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”
units.rightText: On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”

units.leftText: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
units.rightText: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

units.leftText: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
units.rightText: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
rightNotes: 27:1 Or Augustan

units.leftText: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.
units.rightText: We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
rightNotes: 27:2 Literally sail to the places along Asia; Asia was a Roman province in what is now western Turkey.

units.leftText: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.
units.rightText: The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.

units.leftText: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
units.rightText: After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.

units.leftText: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
units.rightText: And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.

units.leftText: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.
units.rightText: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.

units.leftText: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
units.rightText: After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

units.leftText: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
units.rightText: After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

units.leftText: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them
units.rightText: By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them,
rightNotes: 27:9 That is, Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement

units.leftText: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”
units.rightText: “Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”

units.leftText: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
units.rightText: But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.

units.leftText: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking southwest and northwest.
units.rightText: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, hoping that somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.

units.leftText: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.
units.rightText: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.

units.leftText: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.
units.rightText: But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.

units.leftText: When the ship was caught and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.
units.rightText: Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.

units.leftText: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.
units.rightText: Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
rightNotes: 27:16 NE, BYZ, and TR Clauda

units.leftText: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.
units.rightText: After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.
rightNotes: 27:17 Or the sails

units.leftText: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.
units.rightText: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.

units.leftText: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.
units.rightText: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.

units.leftText: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.
units.rightText: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.

units.leftText: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete and have gotten this injury and loss.
units.rightText: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.

units.leftText: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
units.rightText: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.

units.leftText: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,
units.rightText: For just last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me

units.leftText: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
units.rightText: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’

units.leftText: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.
units.rightText: So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.

units.leftText: But we must run aground on a certain island.”
units.rightText: However, we must run aground on some island.”

units.leftText: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.
units.rightText: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
rightNotes: 27:27 The Adriatic Sea referred to an area extending well south of Italy to include the central portion of the Mediterranean Sea.

units.leftText: They took soundings and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.
units.rightText: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.
rightNotes: 27:28 20 fathoms is approximately 120 feet or 36.6 meters.
27:28 15 fathoms is approximately 90 feet or 27.4 meters.

units.leftText: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.
units.rightText: Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.

units.leftText: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,
units.rightText: Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.

units.leftText: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”
units.rightText: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”

units.leftText: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.
units.rightText: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.

units.leftText: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.
units.rightText: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.

units.leftText: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”
units.rightText: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”

units.leftText: When he had said this and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; then he broke it and began to eat.
units.rightText: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.

units.leftText: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.
units.rightText: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.

units.leftText: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.
units.rightText: In all, there were 276 of us on board.

units.leftText: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.
units.rightText: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

units.leftText: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.
units.rightText: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.

units.leftText: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
units.rightText: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.

units.leftText: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.
units.rightText: But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.

units.leftText: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.
units.rightText: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.

units.leftText: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;
units.rightText: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

units.leftText: and the rest should follow, some on planks and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.
units.rightText: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.

units.leftText: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.
units.rightText: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.

units.leftText: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the present rain and because of the cold.
units.rightText: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.

units.leftText: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.
units.rightText: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.

units.leftText: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.”
units.rightText: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
rightNotes: 28:4 Greek Dike; that is, the Greek goddess of justice

units.leftText: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.
units.rightText: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.

units.leftText: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.
units.rightText: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

units.leftText: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us and courteously entertained us for three days.
units.rightText: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.

units.leftText: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.
units.rightText: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.

units.leftText: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came and were cured.
units.rightText: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.

units.leftText: They also honored us with many honors; and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.
units.rightText: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.

units.leftText: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose figurehead was “The Twin Brothers.”
units.rightText: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.
rightNotes: 28:11 Greek Dioscuri; that is, the Greek gods Castor and Pollux

units.leftText: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
units.rightText: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

units.leftText: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
units.rightText: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.

units.leftText: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.
units.rightText: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.

units.leftText: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
units.rightText: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.

units.leftText: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
units.rightText: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

units.rightText: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.

units.leftText: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.

units.leftText: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”
units.rightText: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”

units.leftText: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.
units.rightText: The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.

units.leftText: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”
units.rightText: But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”

units.leftText: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.
units.rightText: So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.

units.leftText: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.
units.rightText: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.

units.leftText: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one message: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,
